best_narrative.headline: Zocdoc: Telehealth Competitors File Federal Lobbying NY Advertising Rules
best_narrative.body: Zocdoc operates a multi-state healthcare directory and marketplace that connects consumers to providers across telehealth and in-person care, creating exposure to state medical advertising and consumer protection enforcement that rivals are now actively monitoring through federal advocacy channels. Four competitors filed federal lobbying disclosures on telehealth topics between May 2026 and the present, signaling that state-level advertising regulation and fee-splitting enforcement are becoming competitive policy flashpoints. Operators in this segment commonly face material exposure given New York's top-three state status for consumer protection and medical advertising rule enforcement. The advertising compliance and fee-splitting exposure merits proactive monitoring as competitor mobilization often precedes state enforcement activity.

Subject: Competitors Mobilizing on NY Telehealth Advertising, Zocdoc's Exposure Dear Public Policy Head, Four of your competitors filed federal lobbying disclosures on telehealth topics this spring, flagging state advertising and fee-splitting compliance as an emerging policy battleground. Given Zocdoc's footprint across New York and California, your government affairs team should map exposure to state medical board advertising rules and anti-kickback enforcement before competitor activity escalates into state-level rulemaking. Would a 15-minute call Thursday work to walk through the regulatory vector and peer positioning? Best,
[Rep Name]

Your policy team should know state enforcement on fee-splitting and medical advertising is heating up before it becomes a compliance crisis. Prospect: We're tracking this internally, but bandwidth is tight on state regulatory work. BDR Pivot: I get it. Ten minutes Thursday, we'll map which states are moving fastest and where your peer risk is highest so your compliance leadership can prioritize accordingly.

The timing of peer advocacy filings typically precedes state-level rulemaking cycles by six to nine months.
